paragraphs: Westlake Corporation is a vertically integrated global manufacturer and marketer of both housing and infrastructure products and performance and essential materials that are designed to enhance the lives of people every day. Our products include some of the most widely used materials in the world, which are fundamental to many diverse consumer and industrial markets, including residential construction, flexible and rigid packaging, automotive, healthcare, water treatment, wind turbines, coatings as well as other durable and non-durable goods. We operate in two principal operating segments, Housing and Infrastructure Products (HIP) and Performance and Essential Materials (PEM). We are highly integrated along our materials chain with significant downstream integration from ethylene and chlor-alkali (chlorine and caustic soda) into vinyls, polyethylene (PE) and epoxy. We also have substantial downstream integration from polyvinyl chloride ("PVC") into our HIP segment for our residential building products, PVC pipe and fittings and PVC compounds.

As a global manufacturer of housing and infrastructure products and performance and essential materials, we focus on delivering value to our customers, creating sustainable shareholder value, and developing a rewarding work environment for our employees. We are committed to produce products that are enhancing the lives of people every day. We do this by providing innovative and useful products while maintaining high standards of customer service and operational excellence with a commitment to managing costs. We continually explore external and internal growth opportunities that complement our existing products and our integrated structure, help us reduce costs by optimizing our asset footprint and improve productivity.
We began operations in 1986 and since then, we have grown rapidly into an integrated global producer of building products and chemicals through effectively executing our growth strategy.

In 2014, we formed Westlake Chemical Partners LP ("Westlake Partners") to operate, acquire and develop ethylene production facilities and related assets. Also in 2014, Westlake Partners completed an initial public offering of common units (the "Westlake Partners IPO"). As of February 18, 2026, Westlake Partners' assets consisted of a 22.8% limited partner interest in Westlake Chemical OpCo LP ("OpCo"), as well as the general partner interest in OpCo. OpCo's assets include two ethylene production facilities at our olefins facility in Lake Charles, Louisiana, one ethylene production facility at our Calvert City, Kentucky site and a 200-mile common carrier ethylene pipeline that runs from Mont Belvieu, Texas to the Longview, Texas site, which includes our Longview polyethylene production facility. We retain a 77.2% limited partner interest in OpCo, a 40.1% limited partner interest in Westlake Partners (consisting of 14,122,230 common units), a general partner interest in Westlake Partners and incentive distribution rights. The operations of Westlake Partners are consolidated in our financial statements. We are party to certain agreements with Westlake Partners and OpCo whereby, among other items, OpCo sells us 95% of the ethylene it produces on a cost-plus basis that is expected to generate a fixed margin per pound of $0.10. We use this ethylene in the production processes of our Performance and Essential Materials segment.

Since 2022, we own an aggregate 50% membership interest in LACC, LLC ("LACC"), which owns an ethylene plant that is adjacent to our chlor-alkali facility in Lake Charles and has 2.2 billion pounds per year of ethylene production capacity. We receive our proportionate share of LACC's ethylene production on a cash-cost basis, which benefits our integrated downstream operations.

We have grown organically and completed multiple acquisitions as we seek to either expand our existing business or add new complementary businesses. In 2016, we completed the acquisition of Axiall Corporation ("Axiall"), a manufacturer and international marketer of chemicals and building products with manufacturing sites in North America, for purchase consideration of approximately $2.5 billion.

In 2021, we completed the acquisition of Boral Limited's North American building products businesses in roofing; siding; trim; and shutters; decorative stone; and windows for total consideration of approximately $2.1 billion. In 2022, we completed the acquisition of the global epoxy business of Hexion Inc. ("Westlake Epoxy") for total consideration of approximately $1.2 billion. In 2025, we completed the expansion of chlorine, caustic soda and VCM productions capacities at our Geismar, Louisiana site. In January 2026, we acquired the global compounding solutions businesses of the ACI/Perplastic Group (collectively, "ACI"). ACI, a Portugal-based manufacturer of specialty materials serving the wire and cable sectors with manufacturing locations in Portugal, Mexico, Tunisia and Romania.

We are continually seeking ways to enhance the safety, efficiency, and overall impact of our operations on our employees, the communities where we operate, and the environment. We endeavor to produce and deliver our products in increasingly sustainable ways, to reduce the environmental footprint of our operations and to develop products with improved sustainability features. To achieve these objectives, we continue to focus on recycling opportunities within our businesses, reducing waste at our facilities, incorporating more recycled content into our products, seeking to incorporate renewable and bio-based materials, and producing products that support greater efficiency and durability.
Our HIP segment is primarily comprised of residential and non-residential building products, PVC pipe and fittings, and compound products made from PVC and other polymers.

We manufacture and sell housing and infrastructure products including residential PVC siding; PVC trim and mouldings; architectural stone veneer; windows; PVC decking; polymer composite and cement roof tiles; PVC pipe and fittings for various water, sewer, electrical and industrial applications; compounds used in various housing, medical and automobile products; and a variety of consumer and commercial products such as landscape edging; industrial, home and office matting; marine dock edging; and masonry joint controls.

Our HIP business consists of several product groups including: (i) exterior and interior building products, which includes siding, trim and mouldings, stone, roofing, windows and outdoor living products; (ii) PVC pipe, specialty PVC pipe and fittings; and (iii) compounds primarily made from PVC. Many of our products are made from PVC, including PVC products for water and sewer systems and home and light commercial applications for siding, trim and mouldings, outdoor living products, windows and PVC compounds.

Siding. Our siding products include insulated siding and vinyl siding and accessory products. Additionally, we offer premium siding products such as Celect® Cellular Composite Siding, TruExterior® Siding and Cedar Renditions™ Siding. Our siding business is also a leader in non-wood shutters and siding accessories along with an array of specialty tools to aid installation. Our brands include Royal® Siding, Portsmouth® Shake and Shingle, Foundry® Specialty Siding, TruExterior Siding & Trim, Celect Cellular Exteriors, Mid-America® Exteriors, Tapco Tools®, and many more.

Trim and Mouldings. We offer a wide variety of trim and moulding products, including exterior and interior products for homes, multi-family and light commercial structures that are used as substitute for wood and wood composite offerings. Our brands include Royal Trim and Mouldings, TruExterior Siding & Trim, and Kleer Lumber®, among others.

Stone. We are a leader in the masonry stone veneer category, with both mortar applied products and mechanically fastened products that are used as a substitute for stone on exterior walls and accents as well as in interior applications such as fireplaces, kitchens and bathrooms. Our stone brands include Cultured Stone®, Eldorado Stone®, Versetta Stone®, StoneCraft Industries® and Dutch Quality Stone®.

headings: Risk Related to Business, Industry and Operations
Cyclicality in the petrochemical industry has in the past, and may in the future, result in reduced operating margins or operating losses.

Our Performance and Essential Materials business could suffer if commodity product exports by other countries significantly increase or are sold in global markets in violation of international fair trade laws.
We sell most of our commodity products in highly competitive markets and face significant competition and price pressure.
Our operations and assets are subject to climate-related risks such as hurricanes or other weather events that may adversely affect our results of operations and cash flows.
External factors beyond our control can cause fluctuations in demand for our products and in our prices and margins, which may negatively affect our results of operations and cash flows.
The North American housing market may remain depressed or decline further, and any such continuation or decline in the homebuilding industry may adversely affect our operating results.
Our inability to compete successfully may reduce our operating profits.
Our production facilities process some volatile and hazardous materials that subject us to operating risks that could adversely affect our operating results.
We rely on a limited number of outside suppliers for specified feedstocks and services.
We rely heavily on third party transportation, which subjects us to risks and costs that we cannot control. Such risks and costs may materially adversely affect our operations.
Capital projects are subject to risks, including delays and cost overruns, which could have an adverse impact on our financial condition and results of operations.
Public and investor sentiment towards climate change and other sustainability matters could adversely affect our cost of capital and the price of our common stock.
Our participation in joint ventures and similar arrangements exposes us to a number of risks, including risks of shared control.
Our operations could be adversely affected by labor relations.
If we are unable to execute our cost reduction plans successfully, our total operating costs may be greater than expected, which may adversely affect our profitability.
If our goodwill or other long-lived assets become impaired in the future, we may be required to record non-cash charges to earnings, which could be significant.
Failure to adequately protect critical data and technology systems could materially affect our operations.
Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates could affect our consolidated financial results.
Our property insurance has only partial coverage for acts of terrorism and, in the event of terrorist attack, we could lose net sales and our facilities.
The impact and effects of public health crises, pandemics and epidemics could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our operations and assets are subject to extensive environmental, health and safety laws and regulations.
paragraphs: Risks Related to Our Business, Industry and Operations
•Cyclicality in the petrochemical industry has in the past, and may in the future, result in reduced operating margins or operating losses.

•Our Performance and Essential Materials business could suffer if commodity product exports by other countries significantly increase or are sold in global markets in violation of international fair trade laws.
•We sell most of our commodity products in highly competitive markets and face significant competition and price pressure.

•We operate internationally and are subject to related risks, including exchange rate fluctuations, exchange controls, trade barriers, tariffs and duties, political risk and other risks relating to international operations.

•Our operations depend on the availability and costs of raw materials, energy and utilities, and volatility in costs of raw materials, energy and utilities and supply chain constraints may result in increased operating expenses and adversely affect our results of operations and cash flows.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis is management's perspective of our current financial condition and results of operations and should be read in conjunction with "Items 1A. "Risk Factors" and "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" included in this report. This discussion and analysis includes the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 and comparison between such years. The discussion for the year ended December 31, 2023 and comparison between the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 have been omitted from this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, as such information can be found in Part II, "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 which was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on February 25, 2025. The following discussion includes forward-looking statements that involve certain risks and uncertainties. See "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" included within this report.

We are a vertically integrated global manufacturer and marketer of both housing and infrastructure products and performance and essential materials. We operate in two principal operating segments, Housing and Infrastructure Products (HIP) and Performance and Essential Materials (PEM). The HIP segment includes Westlake Royal Building Products, Westlake Pipe & Fittings and Westlake Global Compounds. The PEM segment includes Westlake North American Chlorovinyls, Westlake European & Asian Chlorovinyls, Westlake Olefins and Polyethylene and Westlake Epoxy. We are highly integrated along our materials chain with significant downstream integration from ethylene and chlor-alkali (chlorine and caustic soda) into vinyls, polyethylene (PE) and epoxy. We also have substantial downstream integration from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) into our HIP segment for our residential building products, PVC pipe and fittings, and PVC compounds.

On January 5, 2026, we completed the acquisition of the ACI/Perplastic Group (collectively, "ACI"), a global compounding solutions businesses, for a preliminary purchase price of approximately €92.4 million, subject to certain adjustments. ACI is a Portugal-based international manufacturer of specialty compound materials serving primarily the wire and cable sectors with manufacturing locations in Portugal, Mexico, Tunisia and Romania.

In the fourth quarter of 2025, under our asset optimization initiative, we ceased operation of certain of our North American chlorovinyl production facilities, including (i) our PVC plant at the Aberdeen, Mississippi site (ii) our vinyl chloride monomer ("VCM") plant at the Lake Charles, Louisiana North site, and (iii) one of our diaphragm chlor-alkali units at the Lake Charles, Louisiana South site, as well as (iv) our styrene production plant located at the Lake Charles, Louisiana site. We plan to continue supplying customers with PVC, VCM and chlor-alkali products from our seven other North American chlorovinyl facilities. The total costs recognized in the fourth quarter of 2025 and reflected in the PEM segment operating results as a result of these closures was $393 million, of which $386 million was included in restructuring, transaction and integration-related costs and $7 million related to write-downs of inventory that was included in costs of sales in the Company's consolidated statements of operations. The total cost of $393 million included a non-cash charge of $317 million representing accelerated depreciation, accelerated amortization and assets write-offs, asset retirement obligation costs of $52 million, employee severance and separation costs of $17 million and other plant shutdown related costs of $7 million. We expect to incur additional costs of approximately $25 million in the future in connection with the shutdown, which we expect to complete in 2027. Asset retirement obligations and plant shutdown costs recorded represent management's best estimate based on information currently available and are subject to change as additional information becomes available.

In November 2025, we completed the registered public offering of $600 million aggregate principal amount of 5.550% senior notes due 2035 and $600 million aggregate principal amount of 6.375% senior notes due 2055. We used a portion of the net proceeds from the offering to fund the repurchase of a portion of our outstanding 3.60% 2026 Senior Notes pursuant to a concurrent tender offer for any and all of such notes and to fund the purchase price of the ACI acquisition. See "Liquidity and Capital Resources—Debt" below.

In the third quarter of 2025, as part of the Company's continuous assessment of changes in the macroeconomic environment of our PEM business and associated industry and recent operating performance and updated forecasts in the third quarter of 2025, we identified triggering factors associated with the North American Chlorovinyls reporting unit which comprises PVC, VCM, caustic soda, chlorine and related derivatives assets in North America. Due to the recent operating losses and downward revision of forecasts for the North American Chlorovinyls reporting unit along with negative chlorovinyls industry trends, we performed a quantitative assessment to determine if the fair value of this reporting unit had been reduced below its carrying value. Based on the quantitative tests performed during the third quarter of 2025, we determined that the fair value of the North American Chlorovinyls reporting unit did not exceed its carrying amount. This resulted in a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $727 million taken in the third quarter of 2025, representing all the goodwill associated with the North American Chlorovinyls reporting unit and recognized within the PEM segment.

In July 2025, President Trump signed into law the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ("OBBBA"), which includes a broad range of tax reform provisions affecting corporations. Among other changes, the OBBBA permanently reinstates the "bonus" depreciation provisions that allow for the immediate expensing of 100% of the cost of certain qualified property, permanently reinstates the elective immediate expensing of domestic research and experimental expenditures paid or incurred, and permanently relaxes the limitation on the deductibility of business interest. The OBBBA also modifies certain international tax provisions. We evaluated the impact of these tax law changes and recognized the associated income tax effects in the consolidated financial statements beginning in the third quarter of 2025. At this time, we expect these tax law changes to reduce our cash tax without materially impacting our effective income tax rate.

In the second and third quarter of 2025, due to the sustained deterioration of Westlake Epoxy sales volumes and prices in recent years, we permanently ceased operations of the allyl chloride (AC), epichlorohydrin (ECH), bisphenol A (BPA), liquid epoxy resin (LER) and solid epoxy resin (SER) units at our site in Pernis, the Netherlands. We continue to operate our epoxy units in the U.S., other European locations, and in Asia in order to serve our customers globally. The total costs recognized in 2025 of $247 million consisted of charges for asset retirement obligations of $98 million, contract termination and other plant closure costs of $111 million and employee severance and separation costs of $23 million, which are included in the restructuring, transaction and integration-related costs, and the write-down of inventory of $15 million, which is included as a component of cost of sales in our consolidated statement of operations. These expenses are reflected in the PEM segment operating results. We expect to incur additional costs of approximately $10 million in the future in connection with the shutdown, which we expect to complete in 2030. Asset retirement obligations and plant shutdown costs recorded represent management's best estimate based on information currently available and are subject to change as additional information becomes available.

In October 2025, our 95% owned joint venture Suzhou Huasu Plastics approved the shutdown of its PVC resin unit located at its plant in Suzhou, Jiangsu, China. The decision was driven by the unit's lack of long-term economic viability. We continue to operate the PVC calendar products unit at Suzhou Huasu Plastics facility. We recognized expenses of $9 million in 2025 relating to the closure, which is included in restructuring, transaction and integration-related costs.

In 2025, the U.S. government announced new and expanded tariffs on products imported from other countries, with an emphasis on the countries with which the United States has the largest trade deficits, including China. Increased tariffs by the United States have led and may continue to lead to the imposition of retaliatory tariffs by other countries. Additionally, the U.S. government has threatened, announced and modified, delayed or rescinded multiple tariffs on several foreign jurisdictions, which has increased uncertainty regarding the ultimate effect of the tariffs on economic conditions. Current uncertainties about tariffs and their effects on trading relationships may affect the costs for and availability of raw materials or contribute to inflation in the markets in which we operate. Although we continue to monitor the economic effects of such announcements, as well as opportunities to mitigate their related impacts, costs and other effects associated with the tariffs remain uncertain.

In April 2024, the U.S. Epoxy Resin Producers Ad Hoc Coalition (the "Coalition"), of which we are a member, filed petitions with the U.S. Department of Commerce and the U.S. International Trade Commission requesting the initiation of antidumping investigations regarding imports of certain epoxy resins from China, India, South Korea, Taiwan, and Thailand and countervailing duty investigations regarding imports of the same products from China, India, South Korea, and Taiwan. In May 2025, the U.S. Department of Commerce imposed antidumping and countervailing duty orders on imports of epoxy resins from South Korea and Taiwan and an antidumping order on imports of epoxy resins from Thailand. In June 2024, the Coalition confidentially lodged an antidumping complaint with the European Commission requesting the initiation of an antidumping investigation concerning imports of epoxy resins into the European Union market originating in China, South Korea, Taiwan and Thailand. The European Commission imposed definitive duties in late July 2025 on imports of epoxy resins from China, Taiwan, and Thailand.

Our HIP segment is primarily comprised of residential building products, PVC pipe and fittings, and compound products made from PVC and other polymers. Our sales are affected by the level of new home construction and home repair and remodeling activity, particularly in North America, as well as the decisions of distributors and dealers on the levels of inventory they carry, their views on product demand, their financial condition and the manner in which they choose to manage inventory risk. Since the beginning of 2024, with the stabilization of interest rates, recent interest rate cuts and the possibility of further interest rate cuts by the U.S. Federal Reserve, we expect improvement in the demand for housing products in North America. Performance of our HIP businesses generally reflects trends of building permits and housing starts in the New Residential Construction Survey by the U.S. Census Bureau and the Repair and Remodeling Index (RRI) provided by the National Association of Home Builders (the "NAHB") among others. Although we ultimately expect that the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act of 2021 and the preceding historically low level of residential housing construction that has resulted in an undersupply of existing housing may favorably impact our HIP segment in the long-term, the current inflationary environment impacting consumer spending and priorities and decade-high level of mortgage interest rates impacting consumer affordability are expected to have an unfavorable impact on the demand for housing construction in the near term and, as a result, our products produced by this segment. Our PEM segment manufactures products such as ethylene, PE, chlor-alkali, chlorinated derivative products, ethylene dichloride, VCM and PVC, many of which are used in our integrated vinyls production chain. The chlor-alkali and petrochemical industries exhibit cyclical commodity characteristics, and margins are influenced by changes in the balance between global supply and demand and the resulting operating rates, the level of general economic activity, turnaround activities and the price of raw materials. Since the second half of 2022, we have continued to experience lower prices, increased supply and weaker demand for most of our performance and essential materials products globally. The ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, the conflict in the Middle East, slow economic growth in China and Europe, increases in base epoxy resin exports out of Asia into European and North American markets, lower margins in Europe due to increases in conversion costs, disruption of trade flows due to enactment of duties and tariffs and related uncertainties, overcapacity of PVC resin, polyethylene, chlor-alkali and epoxy, and volatility in natural gas, electricity and crude oil prices could have a continuing negative impact on the performance of PEM businesses.

paragraphs: Westlake Corporation 為一家垂直整合的全球製造與行銷公司，提供住宅與基礎建設產品以及性能與必要材料，這些產品旨在提升人們的日常生活。我們的產品包括全球最廣泛使用的材料，這些材料是許多多樣化消費與工業市場的基礎，包括住宅建設、柔性和剛性包裝、汽車、醫療、水處理、風力渦輪機、塗料以及其他耐用與非耐用商品。我們在兩個主要營運部門中運作，即住宅與基礎建設產品（HIP）與性能與必要材料（PEM）。我們在材料鏈中高度整合，並有顯著的下游整合，從乙烯與氯-鹼（氯氣與氫氧化鈉）至乙烯基、聚乙烯（PE）與環氧樹脂。我們也擁有從聚氯乙烯（"PVC"）至HIP部門的顯著下游整合，用於我們的住宅建築產品、PVC管與配件以及PVC化合物。
作為一家全球製造住宅與基礎建設產品以及性能與必要材料的公司，我們致力於為客戶創造價值、創造可持續的股東價值，並為員工提供有吸引力的工作環境。我們承諾生產能提升人們日常生活的產品。我們透過提供創新且實用的產品，同時維持高標準的客戶服務與運營卓越，並承諾管理成本來達成此目標。我們持續探索與我們現有產品及整合結構相輔相成的外部與內部成長機會，協助我們優化資產規模以降低成本並提高生產力。
我們自1986年起開始營運，並透過有效執行成長策略，迅速成長為一家整合的全球建築產品與化學品製造商。

2014年，我們成立了Westlake Chemical Partners LP（"Westlake Partners"），用以運作、取得與發展乙烯生產設施及相關資產。同年，Westlake Partners 完成了首次公開發行普通單位（"Westlake Partners IPO"）。截至2026年2月18日，Westlake Partners 的資產包括 Westlake Chemical OpCo LP（"OpCo"）的22.8%有限合夥人權益，以及 OpCo 的普通合夥人權益。OpCo 的資產包括兩座乙烯生產設施，位於路易斯安那州拉克查爾斯的烯烴設施，一座乙烯生產設施位於肯塔基州卡爾弗特城，以及一座200英里長的共同運輸乙烯管線，從德克薩斯州蒙特貝爾維尤延伸至德克薩斯州朗維尤，包含我們的朗維尤聚乙烯生產設施。我們保留OpCo的77.2%有限合夥人權益，以及Westlake Partners 的40.1%有限合夥人權益（包含14,122,230個普通單位），以及Westlake Partners 的普通合夥人權益與 incentive distribution rights。Westlake Partners 的運營已納入我們的財務報表中。我們與Westlake Partners 和 OpCo 籤訂了若干協議，其中包含OpCo 以成本加價方式向我們銷售其生產的95%乙烯，預期每磅產生固定毛利$0.10。我們使用此乙烯於我們性能與必要材料部門的生產過程中。
自2022年起，我們擁有LACC, LLC（"LACC"）50%的權益，LACC 擁有一座乙烯廠，位於我們路易斯安那州氯-鹼設施旁，並擁有每年22億磅的乙烯生產能力。我們以現金成本方式取得LACC 的乙烯生產，這有助於我們整合的下游運營。
我們透過內生成長與完成多項收購來擴張現有業務或增加新的補充業務。2016年，我們完成了對Axiall Corporation（"Axiall"）的收購，Axiall 為一家化學品與建築產品製造與國際行銷公司，擁有北美製造廠，收購對價約為25億美元。

2021年，我們完成了對Boral Limited 的北美建築產品業務的收購，包括屋頂、外牆板、窗框與百葉窗、裝飾石材與窗戶，總對價約為21億美元。2022年，我們完成了對Hexion Inc. 的全球環氧業務（"Westlake Epoxy"）的收購，總對價約為12億美元。2025年，我們完成了在路易斯安那州蓋斯馬爾廠區氯氣、氫氧化鈉與VCM 生產能力的擴張。2026年1月，我們收購了ACI/Perplastic Group（ collectively, "ACI"）的全球混煉解決方案業務。ACI 為一家葡萄牙製造商，專門生產用於電線電纜產業的特殊材料，製造廠位於葡萄牙、墨西哥、突尼西亞與羅馬尼亞。
我們持續尋求提升我們運營對員工、我們運營社區與環境的安全性、效率與整體影響。我們致力於以更可持續的方式生產與交付產品，減少運營的環境足跡，並開發具有改進可持續性特徵的產品。為達成這些目標，我們持續關注企業內的回收機會，減少廠區廢棄物，將更多回收材料納入產品中，尋求整合可再生能源與生物基材料，並生產支持更高效率與耐用性的產品。
本公司 HIP 分部主要由住宅及非住宅建築產品、PVC 管道及配件，以及由 PVC 及其他聚合物製成的複合產品組成。
本公司製造並銷售住宅及基礎建設產品，包括住宅 PVC 防水板；PVC 配件及裝飾條；建築石板外牆貼面；窗戶；PVC 木 decking；聚合物複合及水泥屋頂瓦片；用於各種水、污水、電力及工業用途的 PVC 管道及配件；用於各種住宅、醫療及汽車產品的複合材料；以及多種消費性及商業用途產品，例如景觀邊緣；工業、住宅及辦公室地墊；船港邊緣；以及石材接縫控制產品。
本公司 HIP 事業包含多種產品羣組，包括：(i) 外部及內部建築產品，包含防水板、配件及裝飾條、石材、屋頂瓦片、窗戶及戶外生活產品；(ii) PVC 管道、特殊 PVC 管道及配件；以及 (iii) 以 PVC 為主的複合材料。許多本公司產品為 PVC 所製成，包括用於水及污水系統的 PVC 產品，以及住宅及輕型商業用途的防水板、配件及裝飾條、戶外生活產品、窗戶及 PVC 複合材料。

防水板。本公司防水板產品包括保溫防水板及乙烯基防水板及配件產品。此外，本公司亦提供高階防水板產品，例如 Celect® Cellular Composite 防水板、TruExterior® 防水板及 Cedar Renditions™ 防水板。本公司防水板業務同時也是非木質百葉窗及防水板配件的領導廠商，並提供一系列專業工具以協助安裝。本公司品牌包括 Royal® 防水板、Portsmouth® Shake 和 Shingle、Foundry® 特殊防水板、TruExterior 防水板及配件、Celect Cellular Exteriors、Mid-America® Exter, Tapco Tools®，以及許多其他品牌。
配件及裝飾條。本公司提供廣泛的配件及裝飾條產品，包括住宅、多戶住宅及輕型商業建築所使用的外部及內部產品，作為木材及木材複合材料的替代品。本公司品牌包括 Royal 配件及裝飾條、TruExterior 防水板及配件，以及 Kleer Lumber®，以及其他品牌。
石材。本公司為石材外牆貼面類別的領導廠商，提供使用於外牆及裝飾細節的水泥黏合產品及機械固定產品，作為石材的替代品，並應用於室內場所如壁爐、廚房及浴室。本公司石材品牌包括 Cultured Stone®、Eldorado Stone®、Versetta Stone®、StoneCraft Industries® 及 Dutch Quality Stone®。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析係本公司管理階層對我們目前財務狀況及營運成果的觀點，應與本報告所附之「第 1A 項『風險因素』及第 8 項『財務報表及補充資料』」一併閱讀。此討論與分析包含截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日之年度資料，並比較該等年度。截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日之年度資料及比較 2024 年 12 月 31 日與 2023 年 12 月 31 日之年度資料，已自本 2025 年 12 月 31 日年度 10-K 報告中省略，因相關資訊可於 2024 年 12 月 31 日年度 10-K 報告之第 II 項「第 7 項管理階層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」中找到，該報告已於 2025 年 2 月 25 日向證券交易委員會提交。以下討論包含涉及某些風險與不確定性的展望性陳述。請參閱本報告內所附之「展望性陳述之警示聲明」。

本公司為垂直整合之全球製造與行銷住宅與基礎建設產品及性能與必要材料之公司。本公司經營兩大主要營運部門，住宅與基礎建設產品（HIP）及性能與必要材料（PEM）。HIP 部門包含 Westlake Royal Building Products、Westlake Pipe & Fittings 及 Westlake Global Compounds。PEM 部門包含 Westlake North American Chlorovinyls、Westlake European & Asian Chlorovinyls、Westlake Olefins 和 Polyethylene 及 Westlake Epoxy。本公司在材料鏈上高度整合，並有顯著的下游整合，從乙烯與氯-鹼（氯與氫氧化鈉）至乙烯基、聚乙烯（PE）及環氧。本公司亦有顯著的下游整合，從聚氯乙烯（PVC）至 HIP 部門用於住宅建築產品、PVC 管與配件及 PVC 合成材料。
於 2026 年 1 月 5 日，我們完成對 ACI/Perplastic Group（合稱為 "ACI"）的收購，ACI 是一家全球零組件解決方案業務，初步買價約為 92.4 百萬歐元，並受某些調整條款約束。ACI 是一家葡萄牙國際製造商，專門製造特殊複合材料，主要服務於電線與電纜產業，其製造據點位於葡萄牙、墨西哥、突尼西亞與羅馬尼亞。

2025 年第四季，根據我們的資產優化計畫，我們停止運作部分北美氯乙烯生產設施，包括（i）位於密西西比州阿伯丁的 PVC 廠（ii）位於路易斯安那州拉克爾查爾斯北的氯乙烯單體（"VCM"）廠，以及（iii）位於路易斯安那州拉克爾查爾斯南之一個隔膜氯-鹼單元，以及（iv）位於路易斯安那州拉克爾查爾斯的苯乙烯生產廠。我們計畫繼續透過我們其他七個北美氯乙烯設施供應客戶 PVC、VCM 及氯-鹼產品。2025 年第四季因這些關閉而認列的總成本為 3.93 億美元，其中 3.86 億美元包含重組、交易及整合相關成本，700 萬美元則與存貨減損有關，包含於營業成本中。總成本 3.93 億美元包含非現金費用 3.17 億美元，代表加速折舊、加速攤銷及資產寫-offs，資產退休義務費用 5,200 萬美元，員工離職及離職費用 1,700 萬美元，以及其他廠區關閉相關費用 700 萬美元。我們預期未來會因關閉產生約 2,500 萬美元的額外費用，我們預計於 2027 年完成關閉。資產退休義務及廠區關閉費用為管理階層根據目前可得資訊的最佳估計，並可能因更多資訊而有所變動。
2025 年 11 月，本公司完成註冊公開發行 6 億美元本金金額的 5.550% 高收益債券，到期日為 2035 年，以及 6 億美元本金金額的 6.375% 高收益債券，到期日為 2055 年。我們使用發行所得的部分淨資金，用以贖回部分現行 3.60% 2026 年高收益債券，並用以支付 ACI 收購的買價。請參閱下方「流動性及資本資源—債務」部分。

2025 年第三季，根據本公司對 PEM 事業所處總體經濟環境及相關產業與近期營運表現的持續評估，以及 2025 年第三季更新的預測，我們發現與北美氯乙烯報告單位相關的觸發因素，該報告單位包含北美 PVC、VCM、氫氧化鈉、氯及相關衍生物資產。由於近期營運虧損及北美氯乙烯報告單位預測的向下修正，以及氯乙烯產業的負面趨勢，我們進行量化評估以確認該報告單位的公平價值是否低於其帳面價值。根據 2025 年第三季進行的量化測試，我們確認北美氯乙烯報告單位的公平價值未超過其帳面價值。這導致 2025 年第三季認列 7.27 億美元的非現金商譽減損，代表與北美氯乙烯報告單位相關的所有商譽，並計入 PEM 部門。

2025 年 7 月，特朗普總統簽署《一體大美法案》（"OBBBA"），包含影響企業的廣泛稅改條款。除了其他變更外，OBBBA 永久恢復「加速折舊」條款，允許立即列支某些合格資產的 100% 成本，永久恢復對國內研究與實驗支出的選択性立即列支，並永久放寬業務利息的扣除限制。OBBBA 也修改某些國際稅務條款。我們評估這些稅法變更的影響，並自 2025 年第三季起於合併財務報表中認列相關所得稅影響。目前，我們預期這些稅法變更將減少我們的現金稅，而不會顯著影響我們的有效所得稅率。

2025 年第二及第三季，由於近年 Westlake Epoxy 壽命銷售量與價格持續惡化，我們永久停止在荷蘭珀尼斯廠區的 allyl chloride（AC）、epichlorohydrin（ECH）、bisphenol A（BPA）、liquid epoxy resin（LER）及 solid epoxy resin（SER）單元運作。我們繼續在美國、其他歐洲地區及亞洲運作 epoxy 單元，以服務全球客戶。2025 年認列總成本為 2.47 億美元，包含資產退休義務費用 9,800 萬美元、契約終止及其他廠區關閉費用 1.11 億美元、員工離職及離職費用 2,300 萬美元，包含於重組、交易及整合相關費用中，以及存貨減損 1,500 萬美元，包含於營業成本中。這些費用反映於 PEM 部門營運結果中。我們預期未來會因關閉產生約 1,000 萬美元的額外費用，預計於 2030 年完成關閉。資產退休義務及廠區關閉費用為管理階層根據目前可得資訊的最佳估計，並可能因更多資訊而有所變動。
於 2025 年 10 月，我們 95% 股權的合資公司蘇州華塑塑膠批准關閉其位於中國江蘇蘇州工廠內的 PVC 樹脂單元。此決定是基於該單元缺乏長期經濟可行性。我們持續於蘇州華塑塑膠工廠運作 PVC 日曆產品單元。我們在 2025 年認列與關閉相關費用 9 百萬美元，此費用已包含於重組、交易及整合相關費用中。

於 2025 年，美國政府宣佈對從其他國家進口的產品課徵新且擴大的關稅，重點針對與美國有最大貿易逆差的國家，包括中國。美國提高關稅已導致並可能繼續導致其他國家課徵報復性關稅。此外，美國政府已威脅、宣佈、修改、延後或撤回對多個外國管轄區的關稅，這增加了關稅最終對經濟條件影響的不確定性。目前對關稅及其對貿易關係影響的不確定性，可能影響我們營運市場中原材料的成本與可得性，或導致通貨膨脹。儘管我們持續監測這些公告的經濟影響，以及尋求緩解相關影響的機會，但與關稅相關的成本及其他影響仍不確定。

於 2024 年 4 月，我們為成員的美國環氧樹脂生產者臨時聯盟（"聯盟"）向美國貿易部與美國國際貿易委員會提出請願，要求針對從中國、印度、韓國、臺灣與泰國進口的特定環氧樹脂啟動反傾銷調查，並針對從中國、印度、韓國與臺灣進口的相同產品啟動補貼調查。於 2025 年 5 月，美國貿易部對從韓國與臺灣進口的環氧樹脂課徵反傾銷與補貼稅，並對從泰國進口的環氧樹脂課徵反傾銷稅。於 2024 年 6 月，聯盟 confidentially 向歐盟委員會提出反傾銷投訴，要求針對進口至歐盟市場的環氧樹脂啟動反傾銷調查，該產品來自中國、韓國、臺灣與泰國。歐盟委員會於 2025 年 7 月下旬對從中國、臺灣與泰國進口的環氧樹脂課徵確定性關稅。

本公司HIP應報告分部主要由住宅建築產品、PVC管與配件，以及由PVC和其他聚合物製成的複合產品組成。我們的銷售受新屋建案與住宅修繕與翻新活動的水準，特別是在北美地區，以及經銷商與經銷商對其庫存水準、對產品需求的看法、財務狀況及管理庫存風險的方式所影響。自民國113年初以來，隨著利率穩定，近期利率調降以及美國聯邦儲備銀行可能進一步調降利率的可能，我們預期北美地區住宅產品需求將改善。我們HIP業務的表現通常反映美國人口普查局新住宅建設調查中的建築許可與住房開工數，以及國家住宅建造協會（"NAHB"）提供的修繕與翻新指數（RRI）等其他指標。儘管我們最終預期2021年基礎建設投資與就業法案以及此前住宅住房建設歷史低水平導致現有住房供應不足，可能對HIP應報告分部產生長期正面影響，但目前影響消費者支出與優先順序的通貨膨脹環境，以及十年來最高水平的房貸利率影響消費者負擔能力，預期將對近期內住宅建設需求產生不利影響，因此由該應報告分部生產的產品。

本公司PEM應報告分部製造產品如乙烯、PE、氯鹼、氯化衍生產品、乙烯二氯化物、VCM與PVC，其中許多產品用於我們的整合式乙烯生產鏈。氯鹼與石化產業具有週期性商品特徵，毛利率受全球供應與需求平衡變化及相關運營率、總體經濟活動水準、維修活動、原材料價格等因素影響。自2022年下半年以來，我們持續面臨全球大部分性能與基本材料產品價格下跌、供應增加與需求疲軟。俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間的衝突、中東地區的衝突、中國與歐洲經濟成長緩慢、亞洲基礎環氧樹脂出口至歐洲與北美市場增加、歐洲因轉換成本增加導致毛利率下降、因徵收關稅與貿易稅而導致貿易流動受擾、相關不確定性、PVC樹脂、聚乙烯、氯鹼與環氧過度供應，以及天然氣、電力與原油價格波動，可能對PEM業務表現產生持續負面影響。

headings: 與業務、產業及營運相關的風險
石化產業的週期性在過去曾導致營運毛利減少或營運虧損，未來亦可能發生相同情況。
若其他國家的基礎原料產品出口大幅增加，或違反國際公平貿易法規於全球市場銷售，將可能影響本公司 Performance and Essential Materials 事業的表現。
我們大部分基礎原料產品銷售於高度競爭市場，面臨顯著的競爭與價格壓力。
本公司營運及資產受氣候相關風險影響，例如颶風或其他天氣事件，可能對營運成果與現金流產生不利影響。
我們產品的需求與價格及毛利可能因超出本公司控制範疇的外部因素而波動，這可能對營運成果與現金流產生負面影響。
北美住宅市場可能持續低迷或進一步下滑，若住宅建設產業持續低迷或下滑，將可能對本公司營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司若無法成功競爭，可能導致營運獲利減少。
本公司生產設施處理部分易變且危險的材料，使本公司面臨營運風險，該等風險可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司對於特定原料及服務，依賴有限數量的外部供應商。
本公司高度依賴第三方運輸，使本公司面臨無法控制的風險與成本。該等風險與成本可能對本公司營運造成重大不利影響。
資本工程項目面臨風險，包括延誤與成本超支，該等風險可能對本公司財務狀況與營運成果造成不利影響。
公眾與投資者對氣候變遷及其他永續議題的觀感，可能對本公司資金成本及普通股價格造成不利影響。
本公司參與合資企業及類似安排，使本公司面臨多項風險，包括共享控制的風險。
本公司營運可能因勞資關係而受到不利影響。
若本公司無法成功執行成本降低計畫，總營運成本可能高於預期，可能不利於本公司獲利能力。
若本公司 goodwill 或其他長壽命資產未來發生減值，本公司可能需記錄非現金費用至獲利，該費用可能相當重大。
未能充分保護關鍵資料與科技系統，可能對本公司營運產生重大影響。
外幣交換率波動可能影響本公司合併財務結果。
本公司財產保險對於恐怖攻擊事件僅有部分賠償，若發生恐怖攻擊，本公司可能喪失淨銷售額與設施。
公共衛生危機、疫情與傳染病的影響與後果，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生不利影響。
本公司營運與資產受廣泛環境、健康與安全法規與規則管制
paragraphs: 與本公司業務、產業及營運相關之風險
•石化產業之週期性在過去曾導致營運邊際下降或營運虧損，未來亦可能發生。
•若其他國家之商品產品出口大幅增加或違反國際公平貿易法規於全球市場銷售，將可能影響本公司 Performance and Essential Materials 事業之表現。
•我們大部分商品產品銷售於高度競爭市場，並面臨顯著競爭與價格壓力。
•本公司營運國際化，並受相關風險影響，包括匯率波動、外匯管制、貿易壁壘、關稅與進口稅、政治風險及其他國際營運相關風險。
•本公司營運依賴原材料、能源與公共設施之可得性與成本，原材料、能源與公共設施成本之波動及供應鏈限制，可能導致營運費用增加，並對本公司營運成果與現金流產生不利影響。
